trial_title: Chemical and Mechanical Angioplasty for Vasospasm (SAVEBRAIN)
brief_summary:
This is a monocentric randomized prospective trial comparing 2 different endovascular strategies of intracranial arterial angioplasty in case of refractory intracranial arterial vasospastic stenosis :

* chemical angioplasty
* chemical and mechanical angioplasty

eligibility_table.criterion: Non-traumatic intracranial hemorrhage (ruptured aneurysm, AVM, or per-procedural complication etc)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a spontaneous intraventricular hemorrhage due to an arteriovenous malformation (AVM), which qualifies as a non-traumatic intracranial hemorrhage.

eligibility_table.criterion: Ruptured aneurysm, AVM, intracranial arterial perforation or any bleeding lesion secured with surgical clipping or endovascular intervention.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has an AVM but there is no indication that it has been secured with surgical clipping or endovascular intervention.

eligibility_table.criterion: No contra-indication to both CTP and MRI imaging
eligibility_table.justification: There are no known contraindications to CTP and MRI imaging for this patient.

eligibility_table.criterion: Subject or legal representative is able and willing to give informed consent.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is capable of giving informed consent as she is 32 years old and has not been indicated otherwise.

eligibility_table.criterion: Refractory of intracranial arterial vasospastic stenosis requiring an endovascular angioplasty with a severe stenosis defined on CTA or DSA; and/or a significant hypoperfusion defined according to the mismatch profile in stroke or a MTT>6 seconds. The volume of critically hypoperfused tissue will be based on a time to maximum of the tissue residue function (Tmax) threshold of >6 sec using the Rapid (or equivalent) software.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's profile does not provide sufficient information regarding refractory intracranial arterial vasospastic stenosis or the specific imaging results needed to assess this criterion.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a significant hypoperfusion defined by a Tmax threshold of >6 seconds as measured by the Rapid software?

eligibility_table.criterion: Angioplasty by one of the two methods considered as impossible or too risky by the neurointerventionist
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided about the neurointerventionist's assessment of the risk of angioplasty for this patient.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the neurointerventionist consider the risk of angioplasty to be greater than a 20% chance of serious complications for this patient?

eligibility_table.criterion: Inability to obtain consent from patient or patients relatives
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is a 32-year-old female, and there is no indication that she is pregnant.
There is no mention of the need for any other device in the patient's treatment plan.

eligibility_table.criterion: Need to use any other device
eligibility_table.justification: The criterion regarding vertebro-basilar arteries is not applicable to this patient as there is no mention of involvement of these arteries.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient required the use of any additional endovascular devices during the treatment of her spontaneous intraventricular hemorrhage or arteriovenous malformation?

eligibility_table.criterion: Vertebro-basilar arteries will not be randomized because of the difficulty to assess the perfusion volume in this territory, but will be treated if necessary according to our local protocol.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's specific treatment plan and the need for randomization in this context are not detailed enough to assess this criterion.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the perfusion volume in the vertebro-basilar arteries assessable using our local protocol for this patient?
